page: UpCloud PREMIUM-1xCPU-2GB is a budget-oriented virtual server built on the KVM hypervisor. It features a single shared vCPU from an AMD EPYC 9575F processor running at 2.0 GHz, based on the x86_64 architecture. The hardware configuration includes 2.0 GB of system memory and a bundled 25 GB local SSD for storage. The CPU includes advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512, cryptographic acceleration via AES and SHA_NI, and vector neural network instructions.

In benchmark evaluations, the server demonstrates strong single-core capabilities, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance, single-threaded gzip compression, and single-threaded bzip3 decompression all ranking in the top tier. However, due to its single shared vCPU configuration, multi-core performance and overall PassMark CPU scores fall into the lower tier. Memory performance is also constrained, with read-only bandwidth and PassMark memory scores registering in the lower percentiles, though large-block write bandwidth maintains an average profile.

The primary tradeoff of this server is its shared CPU allocation and limited memory capacity, which restrict its utility for parallel processing or memory-intensive tasks. From a cost-efficiency perspective, it offers a highly accessible entry point for workloads that benefit from strong single-threaded burst performance without requiring dedicated multi-core resources. This instance is best suited for lightweight workloads such as basic web serving, single-threaded utility scripts, small-scale development environments, and low-traffic applications.
